lines_note: COMMITTED THIS PASS at 30, and the figure is measured rather than clustered. Every earlier number on this sheet came from the TOTAL column's own ink and moved with the threshold used to group it — 31 in coverage.json 'to the nearest line', 31 at one clustering threshold, and 53, 48, 44, 40 or 38 as that threshold is walked from 35 to 75 px. This pass does not look at the TOTAL column to count rows at all. It fits a line grid to the ENUMERATOR'S OTHER INK — the 23 entries of the four written industry columns, which are read below and close against their own printed footings — and asks which line count that ink supports. Thirty does, at an rms of 4.97 px against 15.9 for 31, 20.8 for 29 and 14.9 or worse for every count out to 38. See line_index, and tools/fit_census_line_grid.py, which re-derives all of it from this file's own column_closure block. The same method on 33S7-9YYJ-5V returned 30 lines at a pitch of 75.86 px; this sheet returns 30 at 75.88. Two sheets of one book in one hand, fitted independently and with no shared input, agree on the pitch to 0.02 px. RESTATED AT 31 BY T-0646, and the grid itself is unchanged. The fit above is a fit to the INDUSTRY columns' ink, and that ink stops at line 30: the four written industry columns close against their printed footings with their last entry at y2796, so a 31st line cannot be an anchor and the fit can neither predict nor forbid one. It fixes origin and pitch, and one pitch past the last anchor - y = 679.5 + 30*75.88 = 2955.9 - the TOTAL column carries a number the first pass did not read as a line entry: a 4 at y2931-2971, centre 2951, residual -4.9 px against the -14.5 px this sheet's own line 30 carries. It is ABOVE the rule that closes the body, which a row-darkness profile puts at y2971-2980 centred on 2975; the printed footing 198 is at y2985-3033, entirely BELOW that rule, in the footer row. So the sheet has 31 ruled lines with an entry and the grid's 30 anchors span the first 30 of them. coverage.json's contact-view figure of 31 'to the nearest line' was right about the count for the wrong reason, and is restated here as measured.
no_horizontal_rules: MEASURED ON THIS IMAGE: the sheet carries NO horizontal ruled lines inside the body. A row-darkness profile taken across the empty slaves block finds exactly two strong rules on the leaf — the one under the printed heading and the one above the enumerator's footer — and nothing between them: the largest excess over local background anywhere inside the body is 7.5 grey levels, against 77 to 211 for those two printed rules. The printed form rules this page vertically only. That is the reason a continuation sheet is hard to index, and it is the thing the reading of 33S7-9YYJ-5S could not name when it reported that 'nothing on the image settles which [row] without re-reading the sheet against a row grid anchored on the ruled lines': there is no such grid to anchor on. Every row assignment on these three sheets has to come from the enumerator's own ink, and the only column with an entry on every line is TOTAL.
form_note: The right (continuation) sheet of the 1840 schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: twelve SLAVES columns (six male, six female age bands); TOTAL — number of persons in each family; seven NUMBER OF PERSONS IN EACH FAMILY EMPLOYED IN columns (mining, agriculture, commerce, manufactures and trades, navigation of the ocean, navigation of canals lakes and rivers, learned professions and engineers); PENSIONERS FOR REVOLUTIONARY OR MILITARY SERVICES (ages, names); six DEAF AND DUMB, BLIND, AND INSANE WHITE PERSONS columns; four of the same for coloured persons; and seven SCHOOLS, &c. columns. A blank cell on this form is a zero and is recorded as 0.

reject_test: How this pass parts writing from paper, stated once so every rejection above can be checked. The component filter in tools/read_census_continuation.py keeps anything 40 px in area and 12 px tall, which on this leaf keeps creases, rule patches and offset smears as well as digits. The separator is INK WEIGHT: over each component's box, the 5th-percentile grey. Every one of the 23 written entries read on this sheet measures 0 to 5. Every mark rejected measures 80, 94, 116 or 126. There is nothing in between, and the four rejections are not a judgement about what a mark ought to be — they are on the far side of a gap of 75 grey levels.

column_geometry.note: MEASURED, not assumed — and this sheet is the one that made the measurement harder. The vertical printed rules are found by CONTINUITY, an x where at least 60 per cent of the body's rows stand darker than their own local background. On this leaf that test also reports a rule at x1267, in the MIDDLE of the TOTAL cell, and the first run of the column finder therefore found no industry run at all and exited: with x1267 taken as a rule, TOTAL measures 117 px against a 68 px industry pitch, 1.7 pitches, under the 1.8 the bracket test demands. x1267 is not a printed rule. It is one of two CREASES down this leaf (the other is at x1199-1211), and coverage cannot reject it — it covers 0.765 of the body's rows against 0.769 for the true rule at x1190. What parts them is continuity of a single stroke: the longest UNBROKEN dark run at x1267 is 164 px, 0.07 of the body, where the rules bracketing it run 623 and 1101 px. A printed rule is one line; a crease is thirty short ones. locate_columns() now retries with the weakest-by-continuity rule dropped when, and only when, the strict test finds nothing, and accepts the drop only if the merged TOTAL cell lands in the same 2.0-4.0 pitch window every other sheet's does. It does: x1190-1384 is 194 px, 2.5 pitches, against 5V's 195 px and 2.47. The fallback does not fire on 5V, whose eight committed column bounds are unchanged to the pixel by this change.

rule_continuity.what: for each x the rule finder reported, the longest UNBROKEN run of dark rows there, as a fraction of the 2345 px body

pen_stroke_rule_dropped.why: reported as a vertical rule by coverage, but its longest UNBROKEN dark run is under half that of both rules bracketing it: a stack of the enumerator's family totals, not a printed line. line_index.method: The 23 entry_y values in column_closure (commerce 3, manufactures 7, navigation of canals 5, learned professions 8) are merged where two stand within 30 px — two pairs do, because two industry columns can carry an entry for the same family — and a straight grid y = origin + pitch*n is fitted to the 21 that remain, rejecting any fit that puts two anchors on one line and scoring by rms residual. The TOTAL column is not used, which is the whole point: the row index and the numbers are then independent, and T-0631 can read a number AGAINST the grid instead of using it to build the grid.
line_index.jackknife: Refitting with each anchor dropped in turn, 19 of the 21 drops still choose 30 lines. The two that do not are the two END anchors, y687 and y2874: dropping an endpoint shortens the fitted span by a line, so each returns 29. No interior anchor carries the result. This is the same behaviour the fit showed on 5V, where 20 of 22 drops held and the two that moved were the ends.
line_index.corroborated_by: 33S7-9YYJ-5V, fitted by the same tool from its own ink with nothing shared between the two fits, returns 30 lines at pitch 75.86 px. This sheet returns 30 at 75.88.

closure_argument.the_coincidence_this_pass_declines: AT 177 THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES, AND IT IS DECLINED. 177 + 7k = 198 has the exact integer solution k = 3: read three of the five matched pairs as 11 and two as 4 and the column comes out at the printed 198. It is recorded here so the next reader finds it already weighed, and it is refused, for three reasons. The five glyphs are the same glyph - 44 to 46 px wide, one component each, the same construction - so nothing on the leaf says WHICH three; picking them would be spending the residual, which is the one move this sheet's reading has refused twice. 33S7-9YYJ-24 commits the matched pair as 4 on a TOTAL column that closes at its printed 201. And T-0645 settled the same glyph the same way on 6H, reading its ten two-stroke figures as 4s against a footing that closes at 144. A rule that holds on two sheets whose arithmetic checks it is not overturned by a third sheet's arithmetic that does not.
closure_argument.where_to_look_next: not on this leaf. Three readings are still low (lines 4, 13, 26 - the 7, 8-rejected 9 and the 6 of 16) and together they cannot carry 21. The remaining explanations are a digit form this book has not yet labelled, a family this enumerator entered on the left sheet and totalled here in a hand the ink mask does not separate, or an error in his own addition - 8D reads 79 against a printed 106, -27, so a footing on these sheets is not infallible — and T-0652 has since applied this key to 8D's six matched pairs, moving that sheet from +15 to -27 and proving no assignment of 4s and 11s across them reaches its footing either. total_column.corrections_proposed: SETTLED BY T-0647, and not in the direction this sheet expected. The proposal recorded here was that 33S7-9YYJ-5V reads a matched pair of parallel slashes as 11 on its lines 2, 3, 4, 6, 9 and 24, that the digit key above says a matched pair is a 4, and that re-reading all six would move 5V's committed sum from 126 to 84. T-0647 measured the six and they are NOT one figure: three of them (lines 6, 9, 24) are 4s and three (lines 2, 3, 4) are two digits, and 5V's sum moved from 126 to 105. Line 3 could not be a 4 whatever its ink says - it carries a commerce 4 and a learned-professions 1, five persons of that family employed, against a TOTAL column that counts persons in the family - and that is what showed the six were not one glyph. The digit key below is not withdrawn; it is narrowed. It labels a FORM correctly and cannot by itself tell one numeral from two digits, because this hand builds both out of two slanted strokes. What does tell them apart is the x overlap of the two strokes' boxes, calibrated on nine closure-fixed figures including three of this key's own: see 33S7-9YYJ-5V's total_column.stroke_overlap_test.
